transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess what brings me in is I keep having these really awful doubts, like I’ve missed something important. A number on the mortgage payment, or some clause in a client proof — I’m a graphic designer, so proofs are kind of my whole day — or even something like whether a door actually latched.

And the frustrating thing is, even when I know I checked it, the thought just barges back in. Like, “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?” It sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, but that’s what it feels like.
When these doubts come up, do you feel driven to do something — like checking again and again, or going through a mental ritual — to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes… yeah, I do. I’ll reopen files I already closed, reread emails, check the online payment confirmation again — sometimes more than again. And with numbers, I’ll sort of say them silently in my head until they feel… I don’t know, “settled” is the word I use.

It’s embarrassing because a simple invoice or a logo revision can turn into hours, and those are hours I can’t bill for. I’ll start out just trying to be responsible, and then suddenly I’ve gone down this whole rabbit hole of checking instead of actually working.
Do these thoughts or rituals ever take up so much time that they interfere with your day — like耽误 work, social plans, or even just relaxing at home?

Yes… work, definitely. I mean, I work from home a lot, and I used to think that was the problem because the laundry’s right there, the kettle, the cat wanting to sit on the keyboard — but it’s not really that.

It’s that something that used to take me an afternoon, like a simple revision, can drag on for days because I keep going back over it. And then I’m missing billable hours, or I have to push a deadline back, which is… not great when you’re self-employed.

One of my longtime clients actually asked me recently if I could still handle basic revisions on time. That really stung, because I’ve done work for them for years. So yes, it’s interfering. More than I like to admit.
